question: The total liability of the monetary authority of the country (Reserve Bank of India) is called the ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Base Money.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Base Money, **also known as **High-Powered Money,** is the sum total of **currency in circulation** and **reserves held by the banks** with the central bank (Reserve Bank of India in this case).
 
• It is the most** liquid form of money** that is used by the **central bank **to control the money supply in the economy.
 
• The total amount of **coins and banknotes** in circulation as well as **sight deposits kept** at central banks on behalf of commercial banks make up base money.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Narrow and Broad Money **are measures of the** money supply** in an economy.

 
 
• Narrow Money includes **cash, demand deposits, and other liquid assets**, while Broad Money includes Narrow Money plus **time deposits** and other less liquid assets.
 
 
 
• **Credit Reserve Ratio** is the **percentage of deposits** that banks are required to maintain with the central bank as reserves.
 
 
• It is used by the central bank to control the** lending capacity** of commercial banks.
 
 
 
• **Currency Deposit Reserve **is the amount of reserves that banks are required to maintain with the central bank **against the deposits** that they hold.
 
 
• It is used to ensure the** stability **of the banking system.
